claims.text: An ultrathin ALD-deposited Ni or Cu–Ni interlayer on W particles will enhance Cu wetting of W.
The ALD interlayer will reduce void formation during consolidation or sintering.
The ALD interlayer will reduce phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
Reduced interfacial defects will improve the thermal conductivity of the W–Cu composite.
The ALD-treated interface will improve mechanical durability under fusion-reactor irradiation and thermal loading.
Molten-Cu infiltration and spark-plasma sintering of W–Cu typically produce interfacial voids and defects.
ALD can form a uniform nanoscale Ni or Cu–Ni interlayer on W surfaces before consolidation with Cu.
A uniform nanoscale interlayer promotes full wetting and metallurgical bonding between W and Cu.
A Ni or Cu–Ni interlayer reduces the interfacial-energy mismatch between W and Cu.
Improved Cu wetting of W suppresses interfacial void formation and phase separation during sintering.
Improved W–Cu interfacial contact enhances thermal transport.
Improved W–Cu interfacial contact increases resistance to irradiation-induced mechanical stress.
The ALD-treated material will have significantly less interfacial porosity than vapor-coated or SPS-produced W–Cu without ALD.
The ALD-treated material will outperform the named baselines in thermal conductivity and mechanical performance under cyclic thermal and irradiation loads.
Spark-plasma sintering is a powder-consolidation method that can operate below the melting point of the main components.
Vapor-coated, infiltrated, and SPS-produced W–Cu baselines display notable interfacial defects and suboptimal high-heat-flux and irradiation performance.
Keeping processing below Cu's boiling point ensures that Cu remains molten without vaporization.
The relevant service environment includes high heat flux, thermal cycling, and irradiation typical of fusion reactors.
Optimal ALD-interlayer thickness, composition, and uniformity are not yet defined.
A no-ALD control processed under otherwise identical consolidation, thermal-cycling, and irradiation conditions can test the intervention.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as an already fabricated W–Cu composite, whereas the intervention must be applied to W surfaces before they are embedded and consolidated with Cu.
